solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pile of plant refuse, etc (11, two words)

blocks.note: surface reading: a plain description of a garden heap
setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word competitors write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle prints only a straight definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's heap where vegetable waste rots down into fertiliser for the soil.

clue.text: Dog released from lead, see, performing jump in snow

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front letter, and being released from it means that letter is let go

blocks.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

explanation.surface: A dog let off its lead is seen leaping about in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLIE drops its first letter, a C, which 'see' playfully echoes in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollie is a jump made by snapping the tail of a skateboard or snowboard, lifting rider and board together.

clue.text: Tree yielding sugary stuff girl put in food mixture

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: mash is a soft mixture, such as feed for animals
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A recipe in which a sweet tree product and a girl both end up in the food.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase up to 'girl': the manna is the sugary stuff, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The manna ash is a southern European ash tree whose bark exudes a sweet edible gum called manna.

clue.text: King got in kitchen garment for king-in-waiting

indicators.note: to get in something is to end up inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a pinny is a pinafore or apron, informal British
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch puts on an apron in the kitchen, doing the chores for his heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Prinny was the nickname of George, Prince of Wales, later Prince Regent and then King George IV.
explanation.definitionFit: As Prince Regent, the future George IV was the heir waiting to succeed his father on the throne.

clue.text: Special accommodation for pets, sparse

blocks.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special
a cattery is a place where cats are boarded

explanation.surface: Specialist boarding for pets is thin on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattery is a Chambers word for scattered or dispersed, here sparse in the sense of few and far between.

clue.text: Mound set up, millions interred

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written from the bottom upwards
something interred is buried, so it lies inside another piece

blocks.note: to put is to set down
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A burial mound is raised with millions of bodies inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' doubles as the word and its direction; the M is then buried in the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tump is a dialect word, chiefly western British, for a small hillock or heap.

clue.text: German captivates this writer, a philosopher's disciple

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to hold captive, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: Hun is an old derogatory term for a German
the setter refers to himself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German fascinates the author, who turns out to be a philosopher's follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A Humean is a follower of David Hume, the Scottish empiricist philosopher.

clue.text: Kite in fanciful film circling small street

indicators.note: something circling goes round another thing, so it encloses it

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's fantasy film about a stranded alien
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A kite in a fantasy film soars round a narrow street.
explanation.walkthrough: The kite is a bird, not a toy; the film is E.T., whose bicycle famously flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The elanet is a small kite, a bird of prey of the genus Elanus.

clue.text: Catches from famous song writer cutting I'm on

indicators.note: cutting means chopping a chunk off, so the named letters are taken away

blocks.note: Paul Simon, the American singer-songwriter
the letters to be cut off the end

explanation.surface: Catchy songs from a famous writer interrupt my airtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul is a Chambers variant spelling of pawl, a pivoted catch that engages a ratchet wheel.

clue.text: Street in fresh research offering emergency shelters (11, two words)

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: fresh means new or recent
ST is the abbreviation for street
RES is a common abbreviation for research

explanation.surface: A street in which new research provides places of refuge in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest centres are buildings opened to house people displaced by a disaster such as a flood or bombing.

clue.text: Mud left in farm vehicle?

indicators.note: one piece set in another lies inside it

blocks.note: a cart is a farm vehicle
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Mud has been left in a farm vehicle, as one might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Clart is a Scots and northern English word for sticky mud or dirt.

clue.text: Pasta, soft little ball fed to moggy, half of it

indicators.note: what is fed to an animal goes inside it, so these pieces sit within the other
half of a two-letter word is a single one of its letters, here the front one

blocks.note: moggy is British slang for a cat
p for piano, soft in music
a pellet is a small ball
one of the two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A soft little ball of food is given to the cat, which eats half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cappelletti are small stuffed pasta shapes resembling little hats, from Italian cappello.

clue.text: Two French articles interwoven in parts of skeleton

indicators.note: interwoven threads cross over each other, so the letters of these words are worked together alternately

blocks.note: une and la, the French feminine articles a and the

explanation.surface: Two French newspaper articles are woven together inside a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of UNE alternate with those of LA, giving U-L-N-A-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulnae, plural of ulna, are the inner bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Clouds suggesting her sagginess, mama must get upset

indicators.note: being upset means being knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother is upset at the cruel suggestion that her figure is sagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her sagginess' is a coy nod to drooping breasts, from Latin mamma.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammatus clouds hang in pouch-like lobes beneath the base of a storm cloud, named after the Latin for breast.

clue.text: Sulks in pub? The opposite – it's high point for Walter

indicators.note: the opposite of the stated order is meant, so the second item goes inside the first

blocks.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone sulking in a pub, or the reverse, reaching a peak of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' reverses the instruction: the pub goes inside the sulk. Walter is Sir Walter Scott, whose usage Chambers tags.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnet is a Scott word for a pinnacle or pennon, the topmost point of a building.

clue.text: Property initially unlet, rickety? House lacks one (flat too)

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
something rickety is shaky and unsound, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the opening letter
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unlet, run-down property: a house missing something, and a flat as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: house and flat are single-syllable words, so neither has a last-but-one syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A penult is the penultimate syllable of a word, which monosyllables cannot have.

clue.text: A bit of a snack? Exercise freak swallows one

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece is taken within the others

blocks.note: PE is physical education
a means one
a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness freak

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic gulps down a single morsel of a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is one small item in a bag of nuts eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Enter song off-key, behaviour worthy of censure?

indicators.note: a song sung off-key has its notes out of place, so these letters are put out of order

blocks.note: to enter is to go in
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Coming in with a song sung out of tune deserves a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are questionable or improper activities, conduct likely to be frowned upon.

clue.text: Embrocation, one chaps wrapped in cotton fibre

indicators.note: something wrapped in a material is enclosed by it

blocks.note: lint is soft cotton fabric for dressings
I is the Roman numeral one
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A rub for sore muscles, applied to a man wrapped in cotton dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A liniment is a soothing lotion rubbed into the skin, the same thing as an embrocation.

clue.text: Cumbrian location, not the first for multinational

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is left out

blocks.note: Tebay is a village in Cumbria, by the M6

explanation.surface: A village in the Lake District counties is passed over by a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England; Tebay is known for its motorway services.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is the online auction company operating across many countries, a multinational corporation.

clue.text: Female name, one changing tons in fashion

indicators.note: changing means altering the order, so these letters are rearranged
pieces placed in another sit inside it

blocks.note: a line is a fashion style or range
the letters to be rearranged
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A woman's name for someone who changes tons of clothes to stay in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leontine is a given name for a woman, a French form meaning lion-like.

clue.text: Disease realist treated with injection of iodine

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so these letters are reworked
an injection goes into the body, so this letter is put inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth patient is treated with an iodine injection for an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a bacterium causing listeriosis, so the name stands for the illness it brings, typically from contaminated food.

clue.text: Toiled first to last for lots of valuable things

indicators.note: the front letter is moved to the end, so the word rotates by one place

blocks.note: to strive is to toil; strove is its past tense

explanation.surface: Someone worked hard from start to finish for a hoard of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Troves are collections of treasure or valuable finds, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: What about wild men's snarl?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: eh? is a cry of what?
men plus the s of the possessive, rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what has caused a wild man to growl.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of men's joins the anagram fodder rather than linking the words; snarl is the verb meaning entangle, not a growl.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl, like enmesh, is to tangle or catch up as in a net.

clue.text: Excerpt from piano nocturne coming shortly

indicators.note: an excerpt is a short passage taken from a longer piece, so the letters run inside the words

blocks.note: letters found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A snatch of a piano nocturne is about to be played.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for soon or shortly, as in I'll be there anon.

clue.text: Mark idiot led by a target for promotion as a whole

definitions.text: target for promotion as a whole

indicators.note: being led by means coming after, so the A goes in front

blocks.note: taken as written
DM is the Deutschmark, the old German currency
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot marked out by a salesman as a promotional target.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the mass public at which advertising and media are aimed, treated as a single consumer body.

clue.text: Ghastly sheatfish etc released from sea I set free

indicators.note: letters set free are let go, so they leave the longer word

blocks.note: Siluridae is the catfish family that includes the sheatfish
these four letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A grisly-looking catfish is released back into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The S, E, A and I come out of the family name wherever they sit, leaving the five letters in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid can mean pale and ghastly in appearance, or shocking and gruesome.

clue.text: One fully exposed and lacking a suit possibly? Clearly!

definitions.text: One fully exposed and lacking a suit possibly? Clearly!

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the following letter is left out
possibly signals that one possible arrangement of the letters is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone completely on show and without clothes, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger read this as a cryptic definition; a commenter found the wordplay: and minus a, with suit, rearranged. 'Clearly!' flags that the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, entirely exposed and with no suit of any kind.

clue.text: Sort of gally-bagger you may spot in cerise wellies

indicators.note: spotting something in a phrase means finding it lying within the words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A scarecrow wearing bright red rubber boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Gally-bagger is a dialect word for a scarecrow; wellies are Wellington boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewel is a scarecrow-like screen of hung rags or feathers used to turn back deer, a kind of bird-scarer.

clue.text: Brussels regular had Parisian frolic

blocks.note: eu is French for had, the past participle of avoir
a romp is a frolic

explanation.surface: A Brussels regular enjoyed a fling in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A Euro-MP sits in the European Parliament, so is a frequent figure in Brussels.

clue.text: It may bring hunter to a standstill, favouring fox at heart

definitions.text: It may bring hunter to a standstill

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something that stops a hunter in its tracks, perhaps because it is on the fox's side.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunter is a horse ridden to hounds, not the person chasing the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Proo is a call, chiefly Scots, used to make a horse stop.

clue.text: Very old woman limping more grips end of them

indicators.note: to grip is to hold tight, so one piece is held inside another
end of picks the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: game means lame, so gamer is more lame
the closing letter

explanation.surface: An ancient woman with a worse limp holds on to the last of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Game for lame, as in a game leg, is in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammer is an archaic rustic term for an old woman, the female counterpart of gaffer.

clue.text: Obstruction translator encountered with bit of a poem?

blocks.note: TR is the abbreviation for translator
a verse is part of a poem

explanation.surface: A translator runs into a block when tackling a section of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of 'a verse' comes from the article the clue builds into 'bit of a poem'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traverse is a barrier or screen set across a passage, such as a defensive bank in a trench.

clue.text: Periods I'm kept in class, backward

indicators.note: backward means read from the rear, so the word is written right to left
kept in means held inside, as after school

blocks.note: a set is a teaching group or class
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slow pupil laments being kept in during class periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Times are periods or eras, as in hard times.

clue.text: Servants as of old feeling taken aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a sense is a feeling

explanation.surface: Old-time servants are startled by an emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Esnes were labourers or serfs in Anglo-Saxon England, a historical word for servants.

clue.text: Meal just about set, wobbling crookedly

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
something wobbling is unsteady and shifting, so these letters move about

blocks.note: a dish is a meal
just means only
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal barely set, its table wobbling unevenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means dishonest, so crookedly is an informal synonym for acting by fraud.
